newsitem.title: UK: Labour to force more Railtrack investment.
newsitem.headline: Labour to force more Railtrack investment.

text.p: A Labour government would use the powers of the rail regulator to bring about more investment in track and signalling, transport spokesman Andrew Smith told the party's annual conference on Wednesday.
"The way forward is to deploy the necessary public ownership and accountability to create a modern railway," Smith said.
"We serve notice on Railtrack that things will be different with Labour. We will make them invest in track and signalling," he added.
On the newly-deregulated bus industry, Smith said, "Labour will re-regulate the buses." He gave no further details.
"We want bus companies competing on service quality, not on grinding down the terms and conditions of their workforce," Smith said.
Labour officials said Smith's comments on rail were a reaffirmation of existing party policy.
Labour has not said explicitly how it would bring the rail system back under public ownership, but the officials said there would be no precipitate moves after the election.
Smith said the choice on rail was not a return to the past, when rail's share of passenger travel and the freight market shrivelled.

"Nor is it the waste and chaos of Tory privatisation...We will use the formidable powers of the regulator and a publicly owned British Rail to meet clear goals -- to improve the network and to win lots more passengers and freight on to rail,"
Smith said a Labour government would deliver an integrated transport policy. It was not against the car but it wanted people to have a real choice when to use cars and when not to.

In a broad-brush confirmation of a transport policy line laid down earlier this year by his predecessor Clare Short, he said local communities should have more say in devising transport solutions and in assessing and designing bypasses when they are needed to relieve congestion and pollution.
Smith said the Twyford Down road scheme in western England was "a hideous monument to Tory indifference" that had desecrated the countryside.
"I give you this pledge -- no more Twyford Downs with Labour. We must design our transport infrastructure to complement, not vandalise, our countryside.
"That doesn't mean no to every road scheme. It means we explore alternatives thoroughly and we improve road maintenance," Smith said.
